name: skupper-durable-filesystem-reconciliation-c8e0
instr:
Skupper cannot durably resume interrupted filesystem work or expose namespace-scoped reconciliation outcomes. Add receipts that retry unfinished work in recorded order without repeating confirmed effects. Keep existing non-Kubernetes filesystem behavior compatible.

Every accepted mutation keeps one `EventID` across attempts and recovery; identities are namespace-isolated. `EventOperation` has `EventCreate = iota`, `EventUpdate`, `EventRemove`, and `EventBasePathAdded`. `EventOutcome` has `OutcomePending = iota`, `OutcomeCompleted`, `OutcomeIgnored`, and `OutcomeFailed`. `EventRecord` contains `ID`, `Namespace`, `Path`, `Operation`, `Outcome`, `Attempts`, `Message`, and `Retryable`; `HandlerResult` contains `Outcome`, `Message`, and `Retryable`; `RecoveryPlan` contains `Events`.

Durable `EventJournal` records live beneath their namespace's non-Kubernetes data location, survive replacement controllers and interrupted final writes, retain terminal history, replay only unfinished retryable records, and prune terminal records without crossing namespaces or removing recoverable work. Handler completion from `controller.NewInputResourceHandler`, `controller.NewNetworkStatusHandler`, and `controller.NewRouterConfigHandler` means the corresponding bootstrap, refresh, teardown, persisted Site-state, or callback effect is observable. Namespace events handled through `controller.NewNamespacesHandler` complete only when creation establishes exactly one owned controller or removal stops
